evidence: Shell/config.sh exports CONFIG_* variables globally and runs validate_config() at source-time — sourcing this file triggers validation and exits the sourcing shell on failure (exit 1 at module scope)

Shell/run.sh calls 'source config.sh' implicitly expecting the config file to either exist or be created by run.sh itself; run.sh also rewrites config.sh with inline heredoc content, meaning two different config formats exist depending on which entry point was used
Shell/Active_Shellference.sh uses 'source config.sh' at the top scope, with module-level side effects: prints 'Configuration loaded and validated successfully' to stdout unconditionally

reporting_system.py executes 'plt.style.use()' and 'sns.set_palette()' at module import scope — these are global matplotlib/seaborn state mutations that affect all plots globally when the module is imported

Student_Teacher.py: module-level code (lines 159-179) instantiates StudentTeacherPOMDP and calls plot_matrices(), run simulation, etc. at import time — importing this module from run.sh inline python -c triggers the full simulation as a side effect of import

Python/run.sh invokes 'python3 -c "from Student_Teacher import StudentTeacherPOMDP ..."' — but Student_Teacher.py executes a full simulation at module scope before the import completes, causing double-execution: once from the prior 'python3 Student_Teacher.py' and once from the import
benchmark_suite.py configures logging at module scope with logging.basicConfig() — this is a global state mutation affecting any other module sharing the same Python process

run_all.sh uses 'cd $lang_dir' followed by 'cd ..' for isolation, but this creates boot-order coupling: if run_language() is called from a directory other than the repo root, the relative cd will silently target a wrong directory

strengths: Shell scripts generally check for dependencies before importing or running, providing guard clauses at entry points
config.sh is clearly separated from Active_Shellference.sh, showing some intent to separate configuration from logic
Most run.sh scripts are designed as isolated entry points rather than modules to be sourced
initialization_coupling.issue_character: The dominant issue is module-level side effects: the Python Student_Teacher.py executes a full simulation at import scope, config.sh mutates global shell environment and validates+exits at source time, and reporting_system.py mutates global matplotlib/seaborn state at module scope.
initialization_coupling.score_rationale: The codebase scores moderately because most shell run scripts are properly isolated entry points, but three significant initialization coupling defects exist: Student_Teacher.py running a simulation at import scope (causing double-execution when Python's -c import idiom is used), config.sh producing side effects on source, and Shell/run.sh creating conflicting config formats depending on invocation path. These are real defects that would cause surprising failures in testing or composition contexts.

issues.summary: Student_Teacher.py runs a full 20-step simulation and generates plots at module import scope
evidence: Lines 159-179 of Student_Teacher.py: 'pomdp = StudentTeacherPOMDP(...)' and the simulation loop execute unconditionally at module scope
Python/run.sh imports Student_Teacher via 'from Student_Teacher import StudentTeacherPOMDP' — this triggers the full simulation as a side effect of the import, causing double execution
issues.suggestion: Wrap all module-level execution in 'if __name__ == "__main__":' guard so that importing the module does not trigger side effects

issues.summary: config.sh calls exit 1 at module scope inside validate_config, killing the sourcing shell process on validation failure
evidence: Shell/config.sh lines 85-88: 'if ! validate_config; then ... exit 1 ... fi' executes at source time
Active_Shellference.sh line 11-13: 'if ! source config.sh; then echo Error; exit 1; fi' — but config.sh's own 'exit 1' will kill the parent shell before this check can run
issues.suggestion: Replace 'exit 1' inside config.sh with 'return 1' so that sourcing scripts can handle validation failure without killing the parent shell

issues.summary: Shell/run.sh creates config.sh with array syntax while Shell/config.sh uses scalar export syntax — the two formats are incompatible
evidence: Shell/run.sh lines 22-38: creates config.sh with 'CONFIG_ENVIRONMENT=("food" "danger" "safe")' using bash array syntax
Shell/config.sh line 9: 'export CONFIG_ENVIRONMENT="ShellActiveInference_v1.0"' uses scalar string syntax
Active_Shellference.sh uses '${simulation[environment]}' from CONFIG_ENVIRONMENT — behavior differs based on which config.sh is active
issues.suggestion: Unify config format: either use only scalar exports or only arrays, and remove the conflicting inline config generation from run.sh

issues.summary: reporting_system.py mutates global matplotlib and seaborn state at module import scope
evidence: Lines 27-28: 'plt.style.use("seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid")' and 'sns.set_palette("husl")' execute at import scope
These calls permanently affect plot style for any module sharing the same Python process
issues.suggestion: Move global style configuration into the main() function or an explicit initialize_plots() function called at entrypoint rather than at import scope

issues.summary: run_all.sh uses relative 'cd $lang_dir / cd ..' pattern that breaks if not invoked from the repo root
evidence: run_all.sh line 68: 'cd "$lang_dir"' followed by line 74: 'cd ..' — assumes cwd is always the repo root
run_language() has no cwd guard; calling it from a subdirectory would navigate to a wrong directory silently
issues.suggestion: Capture the script's directory at startup with 'SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)' and use absolute paths for all cd operations

root_causes: Python scripts structured as executable notebooks rather than proper modules — no __main__ guards cause widespread import-time side effects
Shell config.sh designed to be run as a script but used as a sourced library — the exit/return distinction creates fragile coupling
likely_symptoms: Double execution of simulation when Python -c import idiom is used
Parent shell process killed when config validation fails (instead of handling the error)
possible_false_positives: benchmark_suite.py's logging.basicConfig() — this is standard library initialization and in the skip list
